changes.feedback: Two issues must be fixed: (1) actionPerformed() is a public method but has no test. Add at least one test that calls ss.actionPerformed(new ActionEvent(ss, ActionEvent.ACTION_PERFORMED, "")) with an appropriate state (e.g., COOL with room.temp > coolTemp) and verifies the resulting AC/heater state, confirming it delegates to timerOff(). (2) testBVATimerOffCoolAcWasOffTempAboveCool is a duplicate of testBVATimerOffCoolTempPlusOne (same state, same temp=coolTemp+1, same initial ac.isOn=false, same assertion); remove one. Similarly, testBVATimerOffHeatHeaterWasOffTempBelowHeat is a duplicate of testBVATimerOffHeatTempMinusOne (same state, same temp=heatTemp-1, same initial heater.isOn=false, same assertion); remove one.

Two tests violate the EP rule that representative values must come from the MIDDLE of each class, not its edges: (1) testEPTimerOffCoolRoomTempEqualCoolTemp uses room.temp=68, which is the exact boundary between the 'temp>coolTemp' and 'temp<=coolTemp' partitions — this is a boundary value, not a middle-of-class representative, and it duplicates the partition already covered by testEPTimerOffCoolRoomTempAtOrBelowCoolTemp (temp=65). Remove this test. (2) testEPTimerOffHeatRoomTempEqualHeatTemp uses room.temp=77, which is the exact boundary between the 'temp<heatTemp' and 'temp>=heatTemp' partitions — same problem, duplicating the partition already covered by testEPTimerOffHeatRoomTempAtOrAboveHeatTemp (temp=80). Remove this test. Each partition needs exactly one test with a middle value; boundary values belong to boundary value analysis, not EP.

changes.feedback: 1. testBVATimerOffStateOff has an incorrect comment: it says 'no case match for OFF in switch' but timerOff() does have 'case OFF: break;' — the comment must be corrected to reflect that the OFF case exists and does nothing (break). 2. Technique Check 3 violation: the state variable (OFF=0, COOL=1, HEAT=2) is used only in switch statements with discrete cases, not in a numeric range comparison, so treating it as a MIN..MAX range and adding tests for state=-1 and state=3 are invented boundaries with no corresponding numeric comparison or range in the source. These tests (testBVACoolStateInvalidBelowMin, testBVAHeatStateInvalidAboveMax, testBVAOffStateInvalidBelowMin, testBVATimerOffStateInvalidAboveMax, testBVATimerOffStateInvalidBelowMin) must be removed.

changes.feedback: Multiple duplicate tests must be removed or consolidated: (1) testBVACoolTimerStartsFromOff is a duplicate of testBVACoolFromOffStateMin — both set state=OFF, call cool(), and assert timer.isRunning(); merge them. (2) testBVAHeatTimerStartsFromOff is a duplicate of testBVAHeatFromOffStateMin — same reason; merge them. (3) testBVAOffTimerStopsFromCool is a duplicate of testBVAOffFromCoolStateMiddle — both set state=COOL, start timer, call off(), and assert timer not running; merge them. (4) testBVAOffTimerStopsFromHeat is a duplicate of testBVAOffFromHeatStateMax — same reason; merge them. (5) The four actionPerformed tests are duplicates of existing timerOff boundary tests: testBVAActionPerformedCoolTempAboveCoolTemp duplicates testBVATimerOffCoolTempPlusOne, testBVAActionPerformedCoolTempAtCoolBoundary duplicates testBVATimerOffCoolTempAtBoundary, testBVAActionPerformedHeatTempBelowHeatTemp duplicates testBVATimerOffHeatTempMinusOne, and testBVAActionPerformedHeatTempAtHeatBoundary duplicates testBVATimerOffHeatTempAtBoundary. Since actionPerformed() must be covered, keep exactly one actionPerformed test using a boundary value not already exercised by a timerOff test (e.g., state=OFF with any temp, verifying no device changes), and remove the redundant ones.
